title: Arkan al-Islam in a Hadith Nabawi

text_simplified: This text explains a hadith nabawi about the arkan (pillars) of Islam and the importance of Salah, Zakat, and Jihad. The hadith clarifies that the foundation of the religion is Islam, its pillar is Salah, and its peak is Jihad. It also shows that whoever fulfills the obligations and is sincere to Allah will enter Jannah and be far from the Fire.

review_defects.english: Arkan al-Islam in a Hadith Nabawi
review_defects.why: The title transliterates 'Arkan al-Islam' and 'Hadith Nabawi' instead of translating them as 'Pillars of Islam' and 'Prophetic hadith'. The body text translates 'arkan' as 'pillars' but the title does not, creating inconsistency. 'Nabawi' is an Arabic adjective that should be rendered 'Prophetic' in English.
The Arabic 'الجنة' is transliterated as 'Jannah' while the paired term 'النار' is translated as 'the Fire'. This is inconsistent treatment of Islamic terms within the same document.
